CVE-2025-39682.title: tls: fix handling of zero-length records on the rx_list
CVE-2025-39682.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tls: fix handling of zero-length records on the rx_list

Each recvmsg() call must process either
- only contiguous DATA records (any number of them)
- one non-DATA record

If the next record has different type than what has already been
processed we break out of the main processing loop. If the record
has already been decrypted (which may be the case for TLS 1.3 where
we don't know type until decryption) we queue the pending record
to the rx_list. Next recvmsg() will pick it up from there.

Queuing the skb to rx_list after zero-copy decrypt is not possible,
since in that case we decrypted directly to the user space buffer,
and we don't have an skb to queue (darg.skb points to the ciphertext
skb for access to metadata like length).

Only data records are allowed zero-copy, and we break the processing
loop after each non-data record. So we should never zero-copy and
then find out that the record type has changed. The…

CVE-2026-137596.description: A server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw was found in KubeVirt's decentralized live migration. The connectURL field of a VirtualMachineInstanceMigration object is not validated at admission, and the privileged synchronization-controller dials the attacker-specified URL. Connection and DNS errors from the dial are exposed in a condition readable in the tenant's namespace. A user with the kubevirt.io:migrate role (a role designed for tenant delegation) can use this behavior as a blind network-reconnaissance oracle to determine the existence and connectivity of internal hosts and ports from the controller's network vantage, including services isolated from the tenant by network policy. TLS certificate pinning prevents session completion with non-KubeVirt hosts, limiting the impact to information disclosure of internal network topology; no data content, integrity, or availability impact is possible.

CVE-2026-59698.title: ex_aws normalizes .. in S3 object keys client-side, allowing bucket or key-prefix escape
CVE-2026-59698.description:
Relative path traversal in ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 object key to escape the intended bucket or key prefix.

When ex_aws builds a path-style S3 request, ExAws.Operation.S3.add_bucket_to_path/2 in lib/ex_aws/operation/s3.ex joins the bucket name and the object key into a single path string and then normalizes it, collapsing . and .. segments the way a filesystem path would. Because the bucket is the first segment of the combined string, a leading ../ in the object key pops the bucket off the path. With bucket mybucket and a key of ../victim/secret.txt, the combined /mybucket/../victim/secret.txt normalizes to /victim/secret.txt, so the request (signed with the application's own credentials) is sent to bucket victim. The same mechanism collapses ../ within a key, defeating any isolation an application enforces by prepending a trusted prefix.

Only the default path-style configuration is affected; requests built with virtual_host: true do not run this normalization.…

xfrm: retry inexact policy lookup after node reinsertion

inexact tree nodes between those operations:

lookup policy insertion
------ ----------------
find inexact candidates
save obsolete hlist head
write_seqcount_begin(&bin->count)

write_seqcount_end(&bin->count)

The merge immediately reinserts the same hlist node into the surviving
tree node. RCU keeps the policy alive, but it does not provide a
consistent view while its list node is moved. A lookup that selected the
obsolete list can observe it empty. A lookup already traversing a moved
policy can instead follow the next pointer rewritten by the reinsertion.
